clue.text: Deprive of air to end resistance

definitions.meaning: in chemistry, to strip oxygen out of a compound
to force a fortress or rebel army into submission, to subdue it

explanation.surface: Someone is to be smothered until they stop struggling.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemists use the verb for removing oxygen from a substance, and soldiers once used it for compelling a besieged town to surrender.

clue.text: Sort of institution where the Terracotta Army trained?

definitions.text: Sort of institution where the Terracotta Army trained?

parts.words: Sort of institution where the Terracotta Army trained
parts.note: the Terracotta Army is China's buried host of baked-clay soldiers, so a joke pictures their college as built of fired red clay blocks

explanation.surface: A history quiz asks what academy turned out China's clay warriors.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain's civic universities founded in the late 19th and early 20th centuries are nicknamed for their building material, in contrast to the ancient stone colleges of Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a newer British university, as opposed to an ancient one, and literally fired clay is what terracotta is.

clue.text: Sprinkler for ship

definitions.meaning: a kitchen shaker for dusting flour or sugar over food
a vessel that scoops mud and silt from a riverbed or harbour

explanation.surface: A garden sprinkler is being swapped for a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A flour shaker is one kind, and a boat that deepens channels by scooping the bottom is the other.

clue.text: Scarf not appreciated by man covered in sores

definitions.text: not appreciated by man covered in sores
definitions.meaning: Job, the Biblical sufferer covered in boils, was visited by friends whose consolation only made him feel worse

explanation.surface: A gift scarf goes down badly with a man suffering from a skin complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'Job's comforter' is proverbial for someone whose attempts to console only add to the distress.
explanation.definitionFit: A woollen muffler is one sense; the friends who consoled the afflicted Job, unhelpfully, are the other.

clue.text: Glance at the fixtures — not much on

parts.note: to scan a page is to look over it quickly
in British sport a tie is a scheduled cup match, a fixture

explanation.surface: A football fan scans the match list and finds a thin programme of games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not much on' looks like a comment on the sporting calendar, but it describes someone wearing very little: skimpy knickers.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief women's underwear amounts to very little clothing being worn.

clue.text: The vehicle outside needs one replacement body part — it's not a banger

indicators.note: the word for vehicle sits outside, around, the word The

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I
a replacement part is a new one
the heel is a part of the foot

explanation.surface: A garage tells a motorist their old car needs a new part fitting, so it isn't a wreck after all.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang both for an old car and for a firework that explodes noisily; this firework spins and fizzes on a pin instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning pinwheel firework gives sparks rather than an explosive bang, so it is a firework that is the opposite of the loud kind.

clue.text: Have a troubled reign in Africa

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed or upset, so the letters of reign are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A monarch endures a difficult rule somewhere on the African continent.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the location: the answer is a country, and a river, in West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a landlocked West African state and the great river flowing through that region.

clue.text: There'll be some coffee in a moment

definitions.meaning: freeze-dried or powdered coffee made by adding hot water
a very brief point in time

explanation.surface: Someone promises a cup of coffee shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: Soluble coffee powder is one sense, and a split second is the other.

clue.text: Eerie spot in which there's nothing satisfactory

indicators.note: the word for spot holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: to spot someone is to spy them
the letter O resembles zero, nothing
OK means all right, satisfactory

explanation.surface: A creepy place where nothing seems right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spot' looks like a noun, a place, to go with 'Eerie', but it is the verb meaning catch sight of.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ghostly and unsettling is eerie.

clue.text: Propose old man to oversee the interrogation by torture

indicators.note: in a down clue the father figure stands over, above, the rest

parts.note: pop is a familiar name for one's father, the old man
taken as written
historically, 'the question' meant examination under torture

explanation.surface: A suggestion that father supervise a brutal questioning session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Propose' looks like a suggestion in a meeting, but it means asking for someone's hand in marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask someone to marry you is the idiom's sense of making a proposal.

clue.text: Adonis for example had a vision about a snake

indicators.note: the word for having a vision goes round the snake

parts.note: to have dreamt is to have had a vision
a boa is a large constricting snake

explanation.surface: The handsome youth of myth has a vision concerning a serpent.
explanation.walkthrough: Adonis, the beautiful young man of Greek myth, is the type of a gorgeous man.
explanation.definitionFit: A strikingly attractive man is the classic example of male beauty, and Adonis is its byword.

clue.text: Enthusiasm got us into trouble

indicators.note: getting into trouble suggests disorder, so the letters of got us are rearranged

explanation.surface: Our eagerness landed us in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty relish or zest for doing something.

clue.text: This is found to grow poorly in desert

definitions.text: This is found to grow poorly in desert

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the word for desert

parts.note: to rat is to desert one's side

indicators.note: done poorly, the letters of grow come out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A plant that struggles to thrive in barren land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like the sandy noun but is the verb meaning abandon; read as a whole, the clue describes a weed of poor ground.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a yellow-flowered weed of wasteland and poor pasture, the kind of plant that thrives where little else grows.

clue.text: Handle money specially set aside

parts.note: the ear of a jug or cup is its handle
the mark was the former German currency

explanation.surface: Someone deals with funds reserved for a special purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' looks like a verb, as in manage money, but it is the noun: a jug's lug.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve funds for a particular purpose is to allocate or designate them.

clue.text: Vehicle can carry a little weight only

indicators.note: the vehicle holds the next piece inside it, as a load

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle

explanation.surface: A small van has a very low load limit.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'a little weight' as one phrase, but the A goes inside the cart and only 'little weight' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny unit of mass, 200 milligrams, used for gemstones.

clue.text: They qualify, but it's outside the record originally established

indicators.note: the record is set down at the very start of the answer

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: the word it's goes round, outside, the word the

parts.note: the letters of it's without the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some people pass a test, but outside the original official tally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'qualify' is used in the grammatical sense: describing words qualify nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive words or phrases attached to a name, like 'the Great', modify or describe it.

clue.text: Restriction on movement — worker strikes

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
to cuff is to strike with the open hand

explanation.surface: A labour dispute limits freedom of movement, as workers walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikes' suggests industrial action, but it means blows; 'Restriction on movement' looks political but means wrist restraints.
explanation.definitionFit: Linked metal rings locked on the wrists stop a prisoner moving their arms freely.

clue.text: Cow has top of hill to surmount

parts.note: the brow of a hill is its summit
to beat a problem is to overcome or surmount it

explanation.surface: A cow has to climb to the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' looks like the animal but is the verb meaning intimidate.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully or intimidate someone into submission is to browbeat them.

clue.text: Approach with greenery in our hand

indicators.note: the greenery goes inside the word our

parts.note: taken as written
vert is green in heraldry, and in old forest law green vegetation
East, E, is one of the four hands in bridge

explanation.surface: Someone advances holding foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players, or hands, are North, South, East and West, so 'hand' can give N, S, E or W.
explanation.definitionFit: An initial advance or proposal to someone, as in making friendly overtures, is an approach.

clue.text: A plant the Vicar is looking up, narcissus-like

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Rev, the Reverend, is the title of a vicar
Narcissus of Greek myth fell in love with his own reflection, so being like him is vain

explanation.surface: A clergyman is admiring a self-regarding flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'narcissus' looks like the daffodil, fitting 'A plant', but it is the vain youth of myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Vervain is a herb of the verbena family, long used in folk medicine.

clue.text: Get something back from the Inland Revenue? Impossible!

indicators.note: the extracted letters are then read in reverse order
a portion of the following words is extracted rather than all of them

explanation.surface: Hoping for a tax rebate from Britain's tax office? Not a chance!
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue was the British tax authority. 'from' joins the pieces; the run of letters reversed sits at the start of 'Revenue'.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is a flat refusal, meaning not at any time, not on your life.

clue.text: Plain, cheap accommodation for a Brother

indicators.note: the word for cheap houses, accommodates, the brother

parts.note: something vile is low and worthless, cheap
a sib or sibling is a brother or sister

explanation.surface: Basic budget lodgings for a monk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective for simple lodgings, but it means clear to see; 'Brother' suggests a friar, but is a sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plain to see is obvious and in clear view.

clue.text: Accommodation not available at the Royal Free Hospital?

definitions.text: Accommodation not available at the Royal Free Hospital?

parts.words: Accommodation not available at the Royal Free Hospital
parts.note: the London hospital's name contains the word free, so it jokingly could not offer a bed one is charged for

explanation.surface: A London hospital has no beds to offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Free is a real London hospital; in Britain's free National Health Service, a private patient may be charged for a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a hospital bed reserved for a private, fee-paying patient within the state system.

clue.text: A rugby player, too fat to be fit

parts.note: a prop is a front-row forward in rugby
OS stands for outsize, larger than normal sizes

explanation.surface: A rugby forward is too overweight to be in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like a word for physical condition, but it means suitable or pertinent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something apposite or relevant to the matter in hand is fitting, appropriate.

clue.text: Advocate prepared initially to question witness improperly

indicators.note: only the opening letter of prepared is taken

parts.note: to lead a witness is to ask suggestive questions that prompt the answer, improper in court

explanation.surface: A barrister readies a cross-examination that crosses the line.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'leading question' is one that suggests its own answer, which is not allowed when examining one's own witness.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue for a cause in court is to make a case for it, to argue on someone's behalf.

clue.text: Journalist finds aphorism — one for his cuttings

parts.note: a hack is a jobbing journalist
a saw is an old saying, a proverb

explanation.surface: A reporter comes up with a maxim, one for his scrapbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuttings' suggests the journalist's press clippings, but it means pieces cut by a saw for metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine-toothed saw in a frame is the tool used for cutting metal.

clue.text: Hear Orwell make a loud noise

indicators.note: the word is listened to, so the one entered sounds the same

parts.note: George Orwell's real name was Eric Blair

explanation.surface: Listen to the novelist George Orwell making a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: To sound harshly and loudly, like a trumpet or a car horn.

clue.text: Could be fine story, but can't be told

indicators.note: the letters of fine could be arranged as something else

parts.note: a fable is a short moral story

explanation.surface: It might be a lovely tale, but it is unspeakable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something too great or sacred to be expressed in words is inexpressible.

clue.text: Bob sounds so energetic

definitions.meaning: the chiming of bells, as in a bob, a change rung in bell-ringing
vigorous and lively, as a hard-fought contest

explanation.surface: Bob makes such a lively noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name; it is a bell-ringing term. A 'ding-dong battle' is British for a fiercely fought contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-note peal of church bells is one sense; a hard-fought, lively contest is the other.

clue.text: A hint of promotion

parts.note: a scent is a trace or hint of something

explanation.surface: A suggestion that someone is going to be promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: A rise in status or rank is a climb upward, a move up.
